findings: src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp: the batched FlushRunIntervals only changes the early-exit heuristic. Correctness still rests on the Finalize-time ClusteredIntervalsDisjoint(gstate.clustered_intervals, ...) check. lstate.intervals is still appended for every split chunk (lines 966/978) and merged in Combine. If that check fails, MergeRunStores routes all streamed run stores back through the normal combine. An overlap found late (union of two sorted ranges) therefore only costs extra streaming, not wrong results.

Batch flush checks each pending interval against the global map with the same lower_bound/prev logic and inserts them one at a time, so overlaps within a single batch are caught too. Combine flushes whatever is left. Finalize no longer reads run_intervals_overlap for correctness.

src/common/row_operations/row_aggregate.cpp: the template init is used only when there are no destructors (TupleDataLayout::HasDestructor), the aggregate region is at most 128 bytes, and count >= 16. Two zeroed buffers are initialized and compared byte for byte, which catches inits that depend on the state's address or allocate a pointer. Aggregates are the last, contiguous part of the row, so the copy covers [begin, end) including padding. The thresholds are generic and not tied to the workload.

Neither change recognises specific queries, tables or literals. Both apply to any GROUP BY over clustered keys or with many destructor-free states. The author did not run the suite or compare against the disabled clustered path, but I found no input that breaks the logic.
